nodes.content: Expected cumulative squared loss minus minimum expected cumulative loss; continuation relies on Eq. (1.1) and setting on preceding uninspected page.
Allow arbitrary y_t; for a deterministic algorithm no expectation remains.
Regret_T = sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-y_t)^2 - min_{x in [0,1]} sum_{t=1}^T (x-y_t)^2. Described as growing sublinearly with T.
A fixed comparator is the main convention; comparator sequences are postponed to Chapter 14.
V subset R^d; predictions x_t in V; losses ell_t: V -> R; arbitrary fixed comparator u in V.
Regret_T(u) = sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t) - sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(u).

Algorithm does not know u or corresponding regret. No-regret described as at most sublinear and displayed as lim_{T->infinity} Regret_T(u)/T <= 0 for every fixed u in V. Display uses ordinary lim, not limsup.
Regret dependence on ell_1,...,ell_T suppressed in notation.
Some games allow predictions in a set W strictly containing V; this is a qualified variant, not a universal standing relaxation.
Adversary may choose y_t after seeing prediction x_t; no probabilistic generation assumption. Results apply pathwise to arbitrary legal sequences.

For positive T and y_t in [0,1], source identifies best constant squared-loss prediction as x_T^star=(1/T) sum_{t=1}^T y_t in argmin over [0,1]. Claimed immediate, without an explicit square-completion proof.
Tracking stability is the stated reason the past empirical minimizer can work, not a prediction that future resembles past.
x_t=x_{t-1}^star=(1/(t-1)) sum_{i=1}^{t-1} y_i for t>=2; first prediction may be any member of [0,1]. Called Follow-the-Leader.
V subset R^d; arbitrary ell_t:V->R; existence of x_t^star in argmin_{x in V} sum_{i=1}^t ell_i(x). Conclusion sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t^star) <= sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_T^star).
Base T=1: ell_1(x_1^star)<=ell_1(x_1^star).
At T>=2 assume BTL at T-1; target BTL at T.
Cancel identical final summands to reduce target to sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_t^star)<=sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_T^star).
sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_t^star)<=sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_{T-1}^star).
Prefix minimizer x_{T-1}^star has no greater prefix loss than feasible x_T^star.
Transitivity gives Eq. (1.3), hence induction step and lemma.
Regret will be at most logarithmic; minimax optimality/logarithmic necessity is explicitly not proved.
For arbitrary y_1,...,y_T in [0,1], x_t=mean of past for t>=2 and x_1=x_0^star=0.5, Regret_T<=4+4 ln T. Horizon is positive in source's 1,...,T convention; no T=0 logarithmic claim.
Gray unit-width rectangles for reciprocal sum, curves 1/x and 1/(x-1), support harmonic-sum integral comparison.
Replace hindsight minimum by loss at x_T^star and predictions by x_{t-1}^star, then BTL gives Regret_T<=sum_t[(x_{t-1}^star-y_t)^2-(x_t^star-y_t)^2].
Difference of squares expands/factors as (x_{t-1}^star+x_t^star-2y_t)(x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star), <=2|x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star| using [0,1] membership.
Substitute means and isolate the new y_t: 2 | (1/(t-1)-1/t) sum_{i<t} y_i - y_t/t |.
Triangle inequality and y_i in [0,1] give 2|mean_{t-1}-mean_t| <= 2/t+2|y_t|/t <=4/t.
Combine first-round and later bounds: Regret_T<=0.25+4 sum_{t=2}^T 1/t <=4 sum_{t=1}^T 1/t.
Connect reciprocal sum to Figure 1.1's gray area.
sum_{t=1}^T 1/t <=1+integral_2^{T+1} 1/(t-1) dt =1+ln T; stated with Figure 1.1 visual justification.
Combine harmonic bound with regret <=4 harmonic sum to finish Theorem 1.3.
Source proof summary: BTL substitutes cumulative minimizer sequence, while adjacent means approach one another at 1/t scale, yielding sublinear upper regret.
Algorithm has no tuning parameters, can retain running-average summary, and uses no gradients; single data stream. No extra theorem premise.
Lemma 1.2 premises only: V, ell, feasible cumulative minimizers at all prefixes.
Theorem 1.3 premises only: T>=1 implicitly, arbitrary y_i in [0,1], mean-past algorithm, x_1=0.5.
The opening equivalence to Eq. (1.1) depends on preceding page; not reconstructed from memory. Not needed for pathwise theorem route.
Source asserts the mean is squared-loss argmin, but omits square-completion/existence/uniqueness derivation. Positivity T>0 and interval membership are needed; no source uniqueness at T=0.
Convex-average membership x_t^star in [0,1] is used in factor bound and feasibility. No separate proof is printed; derive from y_i in [0,1] and positive prefix length.
nodes.local_scope: For each integer prefix 1<=t<=T, prove (1/t) sum_{i=1}^t y_i in [0,1] from y_i in [0,1]. This is the literal arithmetic expression in S15-minimizer, not an invocation of its still-open optimality characterization.

nodes.content: Passage (4+4 ln T)/T -> 0 is asserted as sublinearity, not separately derived. This yields eventual upper bounds, not existence of an ordinary regret/T limit.
No bridge in these pages proves existence of an ordinary limit for each comparator regret/T from the finite upper bound. Do not interpret the word sublinear as providing that missing existence.
nodes.note: This is an unsupported ordinary-limit inference, potentially false. It is not a universally provable missing lemma and no repair approval is asserted.

hyperedges.conditional_premises_discharged: Inductive hypothesis supplies prefix inequality at T-1.
Uses stated prefix minimizer property and x_T^star in V; these are source premises, not derived regret inequalities.
Both inequalities are necessary; transitivity and last-summand cancellation.
Induction discharges the locally assumed S16-IH at arbitrary T>=2, together with the base T=1. E-BTL-opt references premise fields P-BTL only, not the theorem conclusion.

For each prefix 1<=t<=T, the observation bounds come from the premise-only P-thm13 node. Feasible membership and the minimizer characterization are open obligations G-mean-range and G-minimizer-bridge, not already proved facts. S14-pathwise is contextual motivation, not a substitute for interval bounds.
Specialize V=[0,1], ell_t(x)=(x-y_t)^2; mean characterization supplies minimizer premise for all nonempty prefixes.
Uses initial value 0.5, y_1 in [0,1], and x_1^star=y_1. Only statement premise fields of S16-thm13 are used.

A nontrivial asymptotic control sufficient to relate comparator regret/T to empirical mean is required; the printed upper bound alone does not establish it.
Forward direction must extract one common empirical-mean limit in [0,1] from comparator-limit hypotheses; reverse direction must supply all comparator limits and nonpositivity.
